table1_values.method: d = ATE(pole_a - pole_b) / pooled_sd(orig, cf); p = Wilcoxon signed-rank on pole-aligned pairs
table1_values.sd_type: pooled SD of original and counterfactual scores

appendix_u_values.method: d = ATE(orig - cf) / pooled_sd(orig, cf); p = paired t-test on orig vs cf
appendix_u_values.sd_type: pooled SD of original and counterfactual scores

root_cause: Table 1 and Appendix U compute Likert d using different ATE directions and different p-value tests from the same underlying data. Table 1 uses pole-aligned ATE (formal-casual / verbose-concise) with Wilcoxon p; Appendix U uses condition-aligned ATE (orig-cf) with paired t-test p. The pooled SD denominator is the same. Both sets of values are arithmetically correct given their respective methods — the discrepancy is methodological, not a computation error.

root_cause_details.difference_1_ate_direction: Table 1: score(pole_a) - score(pole_b), e.g. score(formal) - score(casual). Appendix U: score(original) - score(counterfactual). Since each pair's original can be either pole, these ATE values differ in magnitude and can differ in sign.
root_cause_details.difference_2_p_value_test: Table 1: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on pole-aligned differences. Appendix U: paired t-test on orig-cf differences. These test different null hypotheses on differently-directed paired data.
root_cause_details.why_bt_matches: BT values are identical (.562/.541) because BT is computed from pairwise comparison data (trial1/trial2 choices), which is the same regardless of Likert scoring method.

correct_values.rationale: Table 1 values (pole-aligned) are the correct ones for a style bias paper. The pole-aligned direction directly measures 'does the judge prefer formal/verbose style?', which is the research question. The orig-cf direction conflates style direction with rewriting direction and is less interpretable. Appendix U should be updated to match Table 1's method for consistency.
correct_values.recommended_fix: Update claude_crossbench_analysis.py likert_analysis() to use pole-aligned ATE direction and Wilcoxon p-value, matching the method used in Table 1 for all primary judges. Then regenerate Appendix U table from the corrected script.

cross_validation_other_judges.note: Verified Table 1 method (pole-aligned d, Wilcoxon p) matches for Llama-70B (form d=+.010, verb d=+.020) and Gemini-Flash (form d=-.082, verb d=+.051). GPT-4o and Qwen primary results appear to use different source data files (different n after NLI filtering), making direct cross-validation impossible without identifying those exact data sources.
